items.title: Trump formally recognizes Venezuela's Rodriguez government

featured_image.name: Trump warns of imminent action against Cuba at 'Shield of Americas' summit

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Saturday that the United States has "formally" and "legally" recognized the Venezuelan government led by acting President Delcy Rodríguez, deepening a relationship born from the U.S. military operation that ousted Nicolás Maduro in January.

Speaking at the Shield of the Americas Summit in Doral, Florida, Trump said the administration has "been working closely with the new president of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez," adding that "she's doing a great job working with us." He also touted a new agreement allowing the sale of Venezuelan gold and minerals to American buyers, calling it "a historic gold deal with Venezuela."[1]

items.title: Iran hits Gulf states hours after president's apology

featured_image.name: Iran fires more missiles, drones across Gulf region amid US-Israeli attacks

items.description:
Iran launched a fresh barrage of missiles and drones at Gulf Arab states on Saturday, striking targets across the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar — just hours after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian issued a televised apology to neighboring countries and pledged to halt attacks on them unless Iran was attacked from their territory.[1][2]

The contradiction between Pezeshkian's words and the continued strikes underscored deep rifts within Iran's leadership as the war with the United States and Israel entered its second week.[1]

items.title: Trump doesn't rule out ground troops in Iran

featured_image.name: Trump to attend dignified transfer of 6 fallen service members killed in Kuwait amid Iran war

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Saturday declined to rule out sending American ground forces into Iran to secure the country's stockpile of enriched uranium, saying such a move "is something we could consider later" even as the U.S. air campaign enters its second week.

Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One after attending a dignified transfer ceremony at Dover Air Force Base for six fallen soldiers, Trump said ground troops would only be deployed "for a very good reason" but acknowledged the possibility when asked specifically about securing nuclear material believed to be stored in underground tunnels near Isfahan.[1]

"We haven't discussed it," Trump told The Guardian when asked about troops securing enriched uranium. "At some point, perhaps we will. It would be a significant step. Right now we're decimating. We haven't pursued that yet, but it's something we could consider later".[1]

items.title: Chinese scientists use AI to build first chemical map of moon's far side

featured_image.name: China lands Chang'e 6 sample-return probe on far side of the ...

items.description:
Chinese scientists have built the first high-precision chemical map of the moon's entire surface, including its long-unmapped far side, by combining artificial intelligence with data from China's historic Chang'e-6 mission, according to a study published in the peer-reviewed journal Nature Sensors.[1]

The research, led by the Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics (SITP) under the Chinese Academy of Sciences in collaboration with Tongji University and other Chinese institutions, used a residual convolutional neural network to analyze spectral imaging data calibrated with ground-truth samples retrieved from the far side. The result is the first global distribution map of major lunar oxides that incorporates actual far-side measurements rather than relying solely on near-side calibration data.[2][1]

items.title: Trump says Cuba negotiating deal at Miami summit

featured_image.name: Trump says Cuba negotiating deal with him and Rubio | Reuters

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that Cuba is actively negotiating a deal with the United States, making the announcement at the "Shield of the Americas" summit in Miami, where he gathered leaders from across Latin America. Trump said Cuba is "at the end of the line" and that discussions are underway with him and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.[1]

"They are looking to negotiate, and they are in talks with Marco, myself, and several others. I believe that a deal could be easily established with Cuba," Trump said at the event held at Trump National Doral. The remarks escalate weeks of mounting pressure on Havana and follow Trump telling CNN on Friday that Cuba "is going to fall pretty soon," adding that he plans to "put Marco over there" to handle the situation.[2][1]

items.title: Guinea dissolves 40 political parties, including top opposition groups

featured_image.name: Guinea Dissolves 40 Political Parties, Including Main ...

items.description:
Guinea's government dissolved 40 political parties in a late-night decree issued Friday, stripping the country's three main opposition groups of their legal status less than two months after former junta leader Mamady Doumbouya was sworn in as president. The Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralisation, Ibrahima Kalil Condé, ordered the dissolutions for "failure to fulfil their obligations," according to the decree broadcast on state television.[1][2]

Among the disbanded parties are the Union of Democratic Forces of Guinea (UFDG), led by exiled former prime minister Cellou Dalein Diallo; the Rally of the Guinean People (RPG), the party of ousted former president Alpha Condé; and the Union of Republican Forces (UFR), founded by another exiled former prime minister, Sidya Touré.[3][4][5]

items.title: Dubai airport resumes flights after Iranian drone explodes near terminal

featured_image.name: Chaos at Dubai airport after flights suspended following ...

items.description:
Dubai International Airport, the world's busiest hub for international travel, was forced to temporarily halt all flight operations on Saturday morning after an Iranian drone exploded in close proximity to one of its terminal buildings, marking the second time in a week that the airport has come under direct threat from Tehran's retaliatory strikes on Gulf states.

Emirates, the Middle East's largest airline, announced in a post on X that all flights to and from Dubai were suspended until further notice, urging passengers not to travel to the airport. The carrier resumed operations by early afternoon local time, advising only passengers with confirmed bookings to proceed to the airport.[1][2]

items.title: Trump threatens expanded strikes on Iran as war enters second week

featured_image.name: Trump hasn't decided whether to strike Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump warned Saturday that Iran "will be hit very hard" and said the United States is considering striking "areas and groups of people that were not considered for targeting up until this moment in time," a sharp escalation in rhetoric as the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its eighth day with no end in sight.[1]

"Today Iran will be hit very hard!" Trump wrote in a social media post in the early hours of Saturday, adding that attacks would continue "until they surrender or, more likely, completely collapse!" In a separate post, he cited Iran's "bad behavior" as justification for giving "serious consideration for complete destruction and certain death" to previously untargeted areas.[1]
